operations.title: Prime support is intrinsic to norm homology but inherited from the input degree
operations.statement: For d>2, H_d=(Z/d)^(d-2) intrinsically has annihilator dZ and support the primes dividing d, including their primary exponents. Nevertheless d already enters as fiber cardinality and as the scalar in T^2=dT; after forgetting group action the construction factors through cardinality. Thus current norm homology recovers but does not derive primes. For d=2, H_d=0 and homology alone loses even the prime 2.
operations.scope: Explanatory-strength audit of the algebraic regular-fiber norm construction; no physical realization.

operations.title: Same-order cardinality-factorization hostile test
operations.procedure: Compare C6 and S3. Their group laws differ, but after forgetting induced action both order-six regular norm homologies have Smith module (Z/6)^4. Compare d=2, where the homology vanishes and cannot recover 2.
operations.expected_result: Underlying prime support and invariant factors depend only on d. Any same-order pair with different underlying norm-homology Smith modules would falsify the factorization claim.
